# Spec: 001-design-system-shell
<!-- Generated by /speckit.specify -->
<!-- Date: 2026-08-26 | Roadmap: feature 001 | Branch: feature/001-design-system-shell -->

## Overview

Fill `packages/ui` with the identity tokens and the base component set the rest of the
platform is built from: colours, typography and shapes as **CSS custom properties**, the
canonical logo-chip, cards, buttons, chips, XP pips, the responsive header/footer shell, and
the grid. Feature 000 shipped `packages/ui` as a placeholder with its import boundary
already enforced; this fills it.

**Why this is the gate for co-branding.** Identity values resolve from the organization
record, so **zero hexadecimal literals may appear in a component**. One `#EE9DC4` written
into a card is a tenant's identity hard-coded into shared code — it works until the second
organization exists, which is precisely the failure feature 000 spent its whole scope
preventing structurally.

**Scope boundaries.** This feature ships the *vocabulary*, not the pages:

- Included: tokens, fonts, the component library, the responsive shell (header nav, mobile
  bottom bar, menu, footer), the pixel-art rendering approach, and a component workbench to
  view them.
- Excluded: real pages and their content (003), the avatar builder (004), XP/mission data
  (005), the logged-in home (006), per-organization theme *editing* (007). Feature 003 owns
  the LCP budget measurement; this feature must not make it unmeetable.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A developer builds a screen without touching a hex value [P1]

- **Given** `@fablab/ui` exposes tokens and components
- **When** a developer composes a page from `Card`, `Button`, `Chip` and the layout grid
- **Then** the result carries the Fab Lab identity with no colour, font or spacing literal
  written in the page
- **Edge:** a component needs a colour the palette lacks — the token set is extended in
  `packages/ui`, never inlined at the call site
- **Error:** a hexadecimal literal committed inside any component fails CI, naming the file
  and the value

### US2: A second organization is co-branded without a code change [P1]

- **Given** an organization record carrying `theme.primaryColor` and `theme.logoUrl`
- **When** the platform serves that organization
- **Then** the per-organization tokens resolve from the record at request time and the
  shared components render in that organization's identity
- **Edge:** an organization with an empty `theme` falls back to the Fab Lab CITe defaults —
  a missing theme is never a broken page
- **Error:** a malformed colour in the record does not reach the stylesheet; the default is
  used and the problem is reported

### US3: The header behaves correctly at all three design targets [P1]

- **Given** the navigation order decided in round 3
- **When** the viewport is 1440 / 834 / 390
- **Then** desktop shows six tabs and **no menu button**; tablet shows
  `PROJETOS · CALENDÁRIO · AULAS · ARTIGOS`; mobile shows a five-position bottom bar
  (`… · PERFIL`) that **appears on scroll**, plus a menu button top-right with the logo left
- **Edge:** a signed-in user on mobile gets a very small avatar in the header (round 5)
- **Error:** `BIBLIOTECA 3D` and `INSTAGRAM` must **not** appear in the compact bars — they
  live in the menu only

### US4: The logo is the canonical one, everywhere [P1]

- **Given** the round-2 decision that the header chip is the **orange** extruded
  `FAB ● LAB / CITE BAURU` with the cube **between** the words
- **When** any surface renders the logo
- **Then** it uses the shared component, not a per-page image
- **Edge:** other chip colours remain available for posters and non-header material
- **Error:** the pink chip from the old map mockup must not be reachable as the header
  default

### US5: Pixel art renders crisply without a canvas engine [P1]

- **Given** the constitution's v1 exclusion of any canvas game engine
- **When** pixel-art assets (avatars, hero, station icons) are displayed
- **Then** they render through DOM/CSS with `image-rendering: pixelated` at integer scale
  factors
- **Edge:** a non-integer scale would blur the art — the component clamps to integer steps
- **Error:** introducing a canvas/WebGL renderer in this feature fails review

### US6: Only genuinely interactive components ship JavaScript [P1]

- **Given** the islands discipline made binding by the 2026-08-25 benchmark
- **When** a component is added to the library
- **Then** it is a server component unless it has real interactivity (menu toggle, filter
  chips, search input, like button)
- **Error:** marking a static card `'use client'` fails review — it costs bundle for nothing

### US7: A reviewer can see every component without a running product [P2]

- **Given** feature 003 has not built the pages yet
- **When** a developer or the designer opens the component workbench
- **Then** every component is visible in its states at all three breakpoints
- **Edge:** the workbench is a development surface and must not ship in the production bundle

### US8: Text meets contrast requirements [P1]

- **Given** the palette's recurring pairs and the round-2 white-background decision
- **When** text is rendered on any background the tokens allow
- **Then** it meets **WCAG AA** for its size class
- **Edge:** on white backgrounds body text is navy — pink small text on white is forbidden
- **Error:** a token pair failing AA cannot be shipped as a documented combination

## Functional Requirements

| FR-002 | **Zero hexadecimal literals in any component.** A lint rule fails the build on a hex value outside the token definition file | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | **Exactly one colour token is per-organization:** `--color-primary` resolves from `theme.primaryColor` (default rosa `#EE9DC4`) and drives CTAs, active tabs and card titles. `logoUrl` and `heroImageUrl` are also per-organization. **Every other colour is platform-fixed** — the logo chip stays laranja, the hero band teal, the base navy (CLR-001) | P1 | US2 |

Comfortaa ships in-repo (OFL). **Aldo and SquareFont are never committed** — used freely, redistribution undocumented (CLR-002); developers fetch them per `docs/product/fonts/README.md` | P1 | US1 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | No component contains a hexadecimal colour literal | Lint rule, plus a deliberate probe commit adding one — CI must fail naming file and value |
| SC-002 | Changing one organization's `primaryColor` restyles its pages with **zero source diffs** | Two organizations rendered from different records in the same test run; tracked-source fingerprint unchanged |
| SC-003 | A missing or malformed `theme` never produces a broken page | Test with `theme` absent, empty, and containing an invalid colour — all render the CITe defaults |
| SC-004 | The header matches the decided layout at each design target | Assert the **tab-set data** (six desktop in canonical order, four tablet, five mobile ending `PERFIL`) **and** that the CSS contains the media queries that switch them. Whether the cascade actually shows/hides at those widths needs a browser — feature 003's Playwright (see plan § *What these tests can and cannot prove*) |
| SC-005 | `BIBLIOTECA 3D` and `INSTAGRAM` never appear in a compact bar | Assert both are absent from the tablet and mobile tab-set data **and** present in the menu set — a data assertion, so it holds without a browser |
| SC-006 | Every documented token pair passes WCAG AA | Automated contrast calculation over the documented pairs; a failing pair fails CI |
| SC-007 | No component ships JavaScript without stated interactivity | Test listing `'use client'` components; each must carry a reason comment |
| SC-008 | Pixel art is never rendered at a non-integer scale | Test asserting the clamp |
| SC-009 | Feature 003 can build a page using only `@fablab/ui` exports | The workbench composes a representative page from library exports alone |
| SC-010 | The gate set still grows, never shrinks | CI retains every feature-000 gate and adds the hex-literal and contrast gates |
| SC-011 | A hostile `primaryColor` cannot escape its custom property | Test writing `red;} body{display:none` and similar payloads through the REST API; the stored value is rejected and the rendered CSS carries the default |
| SC-012 | **No code path requires a font file that is not in the repository** | Assert that every `@font-face` for a non-committed face declares a fallback stack, and that no import or build step resolves `Square.woff2`. *(Reframed after review round 1: "build with the fonts absent" was tautological — CI never has SquareFont, so that was simply the ordinary build asserting nothing. The real risk is a developer who DOES have the file locally committing something that depends on it.)* |

## Decisions taken while writing this spec

Recorded so the plan does not re-open them:

1. **The palette hexes are definitive.** Render drift in the mockups (teal appearing
   ~`#478E90`) is a render artefact, per the 2026-08-23 decision.
2. **Skill pips show 10 levels**, superseding the 6 segments drawn in the mockup.
3. **The primary button is pink filled with navy text and a hard offset shadow.** The navy
   variant from the v1 mockup and the navy form button from step 2 are both superseded.
4. **The workbench is a development surface**, not a product page — it is not in the
   roadmap's page list and must not reach the production bundle.
5. **This feature does not build the organization theme editor.** It consumes
   `organizations.theme`, which feature 000 already ships; editing arrives with the
   onboarding wizard in 007.

## Clarifications

### CLR-001: Scope of per-organization theming [scope boundaries]

**Decision**: **CTA/accent only.** `theme.primaryColor` resolves into `--color-primary` and
drives CTAs, active tabs and card titles. The logo chip stays **laranja**, the hero band
**teal**, the base **navy** — all platform-fixed.
**Rationale**: `docs/tech-stack.md` already decided **v1 is co-branding, not white-label**,
with the reason recorded: full per-lab identity would need a designer per lab. Recolouring
the logo chip too would leave a half-rebranded page — the shared pixel art and isometric
vocabulary still read as Fab Lab — which is worse than either extreme.
**Impact**: FR-003, SC-002, US2; sets the token layer's split between per-org and fixed.

### CLR-002: Font files are used but never redistributed [integration]

**Decision** *(revised 2026-08-27, PO)*: **Comfortaa and Aldo the Apache ship in-repo;
SquareFont does not.** Comfortaa carries its OFL; Aldo carries
[`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md`](../../../docs/product/fonts/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md) recording a
documented risk acceptance and stating that the repository's MIT licence does **not** cover
it. SquareFont stays gitignored and is fetched locally per
[`fonts/README.md`](../../../docs/product/fonts/README.md).

The two fonts separated once all three sources dafont names were actually checked: neither
archive contains a readme, Aldo's author site is unreachable — but the **embedded metadata
differs**. Aldo asserts **no restriction at all**; SquareFont asserts
`© Bou Fonts. 2011. All Rights Reserved`, the only author-authored statement that exists for
it. Likely FontCreator boilerplate, but a redistribution decision cannot rest on a guess
about which metadata fields an author bothered to edit.

**Rationale**: *(corrected 2026-08-27 — the first draft of this clarification said the
licence was unconfirmed and that ISS-001 gated this feature. Both were wrong. **ISS-001 was
already RESOLVED on 2026-08-25**, the TTFs were already removed from the repo and its
history, and the reason is more specific than "unknown licence".)*

Verified on dafont: **Aldo the Apache** (AJ Paglia) is listed **"100% Grátis"**, and
**SquareFont** (Bou Fonts) is listed **"100% Free"**. Neither author publishes a licence
text. So the two rights come apart: **use** is covered by the listing, while **redistribution**
in a public MIT repository is simply undocumented — and an undocumented right is not a
granted one. Using them and not shipping them is therefore not a compromise, it is the
accurate reading.

**Impact**: FR-005 (nothing visual is deferred); SC-012 changes meaning — it is not a
temporary state to be lifted later but the **permanent CI condition**, because CI has no
licensed way to obtain the two files and must never scrape dafont. ISS-001 stays closed and
gates nothing.

**Consequence this raises, deliberately left to feature 007**: production must obtain the
WOFF2 files from somewhere that is not this repository (the campus VM, a private asset store,
or a mounted volume). Feature 001 ships the token layer and `@font-face` declarations
pointing at a path; **populating that path is a deployment concern**, and the fallbacks make
an unpopulated path degrade rather than break.

### CLR-003: What "tested" means for a design system [scope boundaries]

**Decision**: **Vitest invariants only.** Assert resolved CSS custom properties, component
contracts, contrast maths over documented pairs, the integer pixel-art clamp, and the
`'use client'` audit. No visual-regression tool.
**Rationale**: the constitution requires written justification before a tool joins the locked
stack, and there is none to make here — feature 003 brings Playwright for real pages, and
screenshots are far more useful once there are pages to regress against. Snapshots taken now
would mostly record the absence of the deferred fonts.
**Impact**: FR-020, SC-006, SC-007, SC-008; keeps the stack unchanged.

### CLR-004: `primaryColor` reaches a stylesheet [security]

**Decision**: **Validate twice** — a strict hex pattern on the collection field, and again
before the value reaches CSS, falling back to the default on failure.
**Rationale**: an organization admin controls this value and the REST API writes the same
field, so the admin colour picker is not the only writer. A value escaping its custom
property context could restyle or overlay the page for every visitor to that organization.
Two independent checks is the same defence-in-depth the tenancy guardrails use, and feature
000 measured why it matters: mutating any single layer there left the harness green.
**Impact**: new FR-019 and SC-011; US2's error case.

*No open `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers remain.*
